title.narrative: Activity under preparation Colombia national fixed connectivity with emphasis on fixed broadband solutions for households, companies, and public-government institutions

description.narrative: The proposed investment project aims to provide information, data, and recommendations to establish the basis for a set of public policies and the formulation of investment projects that allow the development of telecommunications infrastructure in peri-urban, rural, and hard-to-reach areas in Colombia.The EUR 200 M corresponds to a potential credit to the Colombian government that would be allocated to finance projects defined within the pre-investment framework and prioritised by Colombia. The goal is to support backbone connectivity and last-mile projects in ten departments. The investment mechanism, governance, and resource utilisation will be determined within the study framework that CAF is developing and in alignment with decisions made by the Colombian government. This desktop study to measure the connectivity gap will be complemented by support from LACIF funds to go further in the structuring of projects, developing pilots and link the communities of the populations to benefit and help to formulate key projects that can be implemented. The EU contribution (EUR 4.6 M) aims to provide information, data, and recommendations to establish the basis for a set of public policies and the formulation of investment projects that will allow the development of telecommunications infrastructure in peri-urban, rural and hard-to-reach areas in Colombia. The contribution will focus on six main activities:1)   Workshops in ten departments of the country to advance with local actors in potential proposals for implementation projects;2)   Structuring projects¿ feasibility based on the results of the workshops;3)   Develop pilots: Implementation of at least four pilots to test new technologies in four territories in remote or difficult-to-access areas;4)   Project financing options: Evaluate different options to finance the projects, which could include public and private financing, and different public-private investment options;5)   Digital skills: carry out training in ten departments in digital skills, focused on vulnerable populations, women, and local ethnic groups;Gender and inclusion: Consulting on gender, inclusion, and diversity to support the differential approach of these communities throughout the project, to get the most out of digitisation.
